open_cases.requirement: The facade gives the second frame of a laced Opus Block a presentation time derived from its explicit zero BlockDuration (1993500000 ns, the first frame's time); RFC 9559 section 10.3.5 leaves later laced frames' timestamps underdetermined and the reference reports none. Report it absent, or mark it derived (container contract rule 1). The exact CodecDelay times (section 11.2) and the present zero BlockDuration (section 5.1.3.5.3 sets no range) remain deviations once the frame is fixed.

open_deviations.reading: CodecDelay is subtracted from the Block time in nanoseconds
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 sections 5.1.4.1.25 and 11.2: the nanosecond CodecDelay MUST be subtracted from each frame timestamp
open_deviations.candidate: reports exact presentation times on the Opus packets, for example 1992500000 ns
open_deviations.reference: rounds them to the 1 ms Segment tick, for example 1992000000 ns; payloads, durations, flags and order agree

open_deviations.reading: DefaultDuration and CodecDelay keep nanosecond precision on a coarse Segment tick
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 section 5.1.4.1.13 gives DefaultDuration in nanoseconds; sections 5.1.4.1.25 and 11.2 subtract the nanosecond CodecDelay
open_deviations.candidate: reports DefaultDuration 125000000 ns and exact presentation times
open_deviations.reference: truncates DefaultDuration to 120000000 ns and rounds the times to the 10 or 20 ms Segment tick

open_deviations.reading: Seek policy the specification leaves open, with nanosecond CodecDelay: the facade replays the Opus preroll before the target
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 section 5.1.4.1.26 has the decoder decode SeekPreRoll after a discontinuity and assigns a seek no landing; sections 5.1.4.1.25 and 11.2 subtract the nanosecond CodecDelay
open_deviations.candidate: delivers two Opus packets before the first wanted packet on their track, each verified against the sequential source and the Block timing oracle, and exact times on the common packets
open_deviations.reference: its seek starts at the cue without those two packets; the common packets carry times rounded to 1 ms and the same bytes

open_deviations.reading: Seek policy the specification leaves open, with nanosecond DefaultDuration and CodecDelay on a 20 ms Segment tick
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 sections 5.1.4.1.26 (SeekPreRoll is the decoder's to decode), 5.1.4.1.13 (DefaultDuration in nanoseconds), 5.1.4.1.25 and 11.2 (CodecDelay subtracted in nanoseconds)
open_deviations.candidate: delivers a subtitle and two Opus packets before the first wanted packets, each verified against the sequential source, with DefaultDuration 125000000 ns and exact times
open_deviations.reference: starts at the cue without them, truncates DefaultDuration to 120000000 ns and rounds the times to the 20 ms tick

open_deviations.reading: Seek policy the standard leaves open: a target between a sync sample's decode and presentation times
open_deviations.clause: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 8.6.1 defines decode and composition times and 8.6.2 sync samples but no seek; the facade lands on the latest sync sample presented at or before the target (crates/isobmff README, Container reader)
open_deviations.candidate: lands on the sync sample presented at 843000 ticks (decoded at 840000) for the target 924000
open_deviations.reference: av_seek_frame lands on the key decoded at 924000 and presented at 927000, after the target
